flags.text: "Render assistant citations as inline badges with a hover and keyboard-focus tooltip by splitting the answer with `AnswerCitationLayout`, keeping the numbered sources list for citations not anchored inline." - Per #244, `AnswerCitationLayout` and its tests were removed during integration (Markdown leads, inline badges deferred to #243), and #245 re-introduced badges differently via `AssistantMarkdown.Render`. This entry describes a superseded implementation as a shipped feature.

"You can rely on the button doing the same thing as the manual controls, so you no longer have to open them for the suggested step." - The facts say the action goes through the same handler as the manual path; they do not say users no longer need the manual controls. The generic controls stay always available.

"Citation badges in chat: Assistant answers can show numbered citation badges with a tooltip on hover or keyboard focus giving source, heading and snippet. Citations not anchored in the text stay in a numbered sources list" - This describes #233's plain-text badge feature (AnswerCitationLayout), which #244 removed in favour of Markdown-led sources lists. The entry duplicates the inline badge feature and describes a superseded implementation.

"Version 1.9.0 brings the full Frontend Redesign into one release. Assistant answers render as formatted text with citations in a sources list below" - Citations in a sources list below the answer was the interim state in #244. The final release, per #245, anchors inline badges in the Markdown answer as well as listing the sources, so this describes a superseded state.

"so times match the ticket detail view and due dates carry your offset." - The facts say the UTC offset stays in the format string so the model expresses due dates with the user's offset; they do not guarantee that due dates carry your offset.

facts.title: feat(web): inline citation badges anchored in the assistant Markdown answer (#243)
facts.description:
Closes #243.

Re-introduces the inline citation badges that #207 first built, now over the sanitized Markdown answer instead of plain text - the last M9 item, so v1.9.0 ships with the badge feature complete rather than deferred.

## What changed

- `AssistantMarkdown.Render(markdown, citations)` anchors a `[n]` badge after the cited passage title and returns the un-anchored citations for the sources list.
- The badge is injected into the **sanitized** Markdown via private-use sentinel characters (U+E000/U+E001). The model's own text is scrubbed of those characters first, so it cannot forge a placeholder and reach the badge swap - `DisableHtml()` + `WebUtility.HtmlEncode` on every citation field are preserved, keeping the `MarkupString` XSS hardening intact.
- Badge carries a hover/focus tooltip (title, source › heading, snippet).
- Citations are numbered by position, so an inline `[n]` and its "Sources" list entry share a number; co-located badges (two passages from one article) read `[1][2]`, not `[2][1]`.
- A citation whose title never appears in the answer stays in the sources list only - no evidence dropped.

## Verification

- 9 new unit tests on `Render` (anchoring, numbering, unanchored fallback, hostile-content encoding, sentinel-forgery defense, closing-quote placement, co-located ordering).
- Full build warning-free; full suite green (incl. `DesignTokenTests` guard and 73 E2E).
- **Real-browser E2E** against Postgres + pgvector + Voyage: asked a VPN/password how-to, confirmed inline `[1][2]` badges render in the Markdown, the tooltip shows on hover, and the numbered "Sources" card stays consistent.

## Docs

- `docs/releases/v1.9.0.md`, `CHANGELOG.md`, `README.md` updated: inline badges delivered (not deferred). Remaining honest limitation recorded: anchoring relies on the model quoting the passage title verbatim, which the system prompt already asks it to do.

facts.title: release: v1.9.0 - integrate M9 Frontend Redesign into main
facts.description:
Integrates the complete **M9 - Frontend Redesign** milestone into `main` and adds the v1.9.0 release notes, so the release can be tagged from a single coherent point.

## Why this PR exists

M9 shipped as two divergent branches off v1.8.0: the first half (#189, #196, #203-206, #228) on `m9-frontend-redesign`, the second half (#207-211, #214-216) merged to `main` during the closing session. Neither branch was a complete M9. This merges them into one `main`.

## Conflict resolutions

- **#228 (category header) was fixed on both branches.** Kept the `main` version (#238: explicit width + uppercase label), dropped the integration branch's narrower width-only fix (#229); deduped the doubled CSS rule to the integration branch's rebalanced 116px column scheme.
- **Assistant bubble: #207 (inline citation badges) vs #196 (Markdown rendering)** rewrote the same render path. Per decision, **Markdown leads** and citations render as the **sources list** below the answer; inline badges are deferred to **#243**. Removed `AnswerCitationLayout` + tests (in history at `4aea178`).
- **#189 (grounding out of transcript) wins** over main's grounding chip: the `Grounding` and `Citations` `ChatEntryKind` cases are both removed (neither is emitted).
- **#204 replaced `FormatStatus(TicketStatus)` with `TicketSignals.Label`**; updated the call sites in `TicketDetailsPage`/`TicketBoardPage` that #208/#209/#211 added.
- Regenerated the OpenAPI snapshot for the #206 saved-views query params (the integration branch had left it stale).

## Verification

- `dotnet build ./ServiceDeskLite.slnx -c Release` - warning-free.
- `dotnet test ./ServiceDeskLite.slnx` - all green: Web 122, Api 267, EndToEnd 73, Application 79, Domain 36, Evaluation 61, Integration 5, InMemory 18.
- OpenAPI drift check clean after regeneration.
- **Real-browser pass** on the merged assistant page: Markdown renders (bold, numbered list, paragraphs; no raw `**`), the composer send button sits inside its panel (#215), grounding is suppressed from the transcript (#189), and the KB-unavailable path degrades honestly. Dark-mode toggle (#203) confirmed served.

## Follow-ups filed

- #241 - ticket search match semantics (ADR)
- #242 - audit dead scoped-CSS rules on Mud component roots + guard test
- #243 - re-introduce inline citation badges anchored in the rendered Markdown

## After merge

Tag `v1.9.0` from `main`, publish the GitHub release from `docs/releases/v1.9.0.md`, and close the M9 milestone.

facts.title: fix(web): wrap board card title so -webkit-line-clamp is not blockified (#216)
facts.description:
Closes #216.

## Root cause
`.board-card__title` sets `display: -webkit-box` with `-webkit-line-clamp: 2`, but the `<a>` was a direct child of the `display: grid` card. Chrome blockifies a grid item's legacy `-webkit-box` to `flow-root`, so the clamp never applied and a long title grew the card without bound.

## Fix
Wrap the title `<a>` in a `board-card__title-row` div. The wrapper takes the grid-item slot, so the `<a>` is a normal block child and its `-webkit-box` is no longer blockified - the two-line clamp with ellipsis applies. `min-width: 0` on the wrapper lets a long unbreakable title shrink instead of stretching the lane column. This is exactly the wrapper approach the issue prescribes.

## Acceptance criteria
- [x] A title longer than two lines is clamped to two, with an ellipsis. *(verified visually with a long-title ticket)*
- [x] Cards in a lane keep a consistent height. *(clamp caps the title; `min-height: 8.6rem` sets the floor)*
- [~] `getComputedStyle(title).display` is `-webkit-box`. *(structurally guaranteed on the browser the issue targets; see note - not observable on the Chrome available here)*

## Verification
- `dotnet test tests/ServiceDeskLite.Tests.Web/` - 97 passing, incl. `DesignTokenTests`.
- **Real-browser check** (Playwright, long-title ticket): the title clamps to exactly two lines (`38px` at `19px` line-height) with an ellipsis, and the card stays a bounded `165px`.

## Honest note on AC3 and the test browser
The available headless Chrome is **149**, which reimplemented `line-clamp` to work on block containers and serializes `display: -webkit-box` + `line-clamp` as `flow-root` in **every** parent context. An isolated test confirmed this: an `-webkit-box` element reports `flow-root` whether its parent is `grid`, `flex`, or `block`. Consequences:
- On Chrome 149 the bug does **not reproduce** - the clamp works even for a grid-item title - and `getComputedStyle(title).display` reads `flow-root` both before and after the fix, so AC3 cannot be confirmed on this browser.
- The fix is still correct for the **older Chrome the issue targets** (where a grid item's `-webkit-box` blockifies and the clamp breaks); moving the `<a>` out of the grid item keeps it `-webkit-box` there. The change is inert and harmless on Chrome 149.

facts.title: fix(web): keep the assistant composer send button inside its panel (#215)
facts.description:
Closes #215.

## Root cause
`.assistant-chat` is a `MudPaper` - a child component. Blazor CSS isolation does not stamp the scope attribute on a child component's root element, so the plain `.assistant-chat { ... }` rule matched nothing. The panel silently lost everything that rule declared: its `padding`, its `display: flex` column layout, and its `min-height`. With no padding, the composer spanned the panel edge to edge and the send button sat flush at the right border, hanging over it.

## Fix
Target the panel through `::deep .assistant-chat` (the scope lands on the `.assistant-page` root, which is real markup, and the descendant `.assistant-chat` MudPaper now matches). The intended `16px` padding insets the composer, so the send button sits inside the panel and the input and button stay aligned in their flex row at any width. Reviving the rule also restores the intended flex-column layout (messages scroll internally, composer pinned) that had likewise been dead.

## Acceptance criteria
- [x] The send button sits within the composer panel's bounds.
- [x] The input and the button stay aligned at narrow widths.

## Verification
- `dotnet test tests/ServiceDeskLite.Tests.Web/` - 97 passing, incl. `DesignTokenTests`.
- **Real-browser check** (Playwright):
  - Before: panel `padding-right: 0`, `display: block`, `min-height: auto` - the panel rule never applied; button flush at the panel edge (`button.right == panel.right`).
  - After (1400px and 520px): panel `padding-right: 16px`, button sits `16px` inside the panel edge (`buttonOverflowsRight: -16`), input and button aligned in the same row.

Note: the dead-rule cause (scoped selector against a child-component root) is worth watching for elsewhere; here it only affected this panel.

facts.title: fix(web): stop the Category header overlapping Due in the ticket queue (#214, #228)
facts.description:
Closes #214. Closes #228.

Both issues describe the same defect: on `/tickets`, the `Category` column header overlaps `Due`, reading as "CategoryUE".

## Root cause
The tickets table uses `table-layout: fixed`, and every column carries an explicit width **except** `Category`. With no width it collapsed to ~47px, so the "Category" header overflowed onto the `Due` column. Separately, `Category` was rendered with an unstyled `tickets-table__th-label` class, leaving it title-case while its neighbours are uppercase.

## Fix
- Give the `Category` column a `140px` width (matching its neighbours) so it no longer collapses and header/body cells stay aligned.
- Render the `Category` header with the same `tickets-table__label` class as `Ref` (uppercase). It stays a static label, not a sort button, because `Category` is not a server sort field (`TicketSortField` has no `Category`); the reason is now stated in a comment.

## Acceptance criteria
**#214**
- [x] `Category` no longer overlaps `DUE` at a 1600px viewport.
- [x] `Category` matches its neighbours (uppercase) and is deliberately not a sort label, with the reason stated (not a `TicketSortField`).

**#228**
- [x] Category and Due headers render side by side without overlap in both themes.
- [x] Column alignment between header and body cells stays intact.
- [x] No spacing/width literals outside the token scale where tokens apply (DesignTokenTests stay green; width is not token-guarded, and no padding/margin/gap literals were added).

## Verification
- `dotnet test tests/ServiceDeskLite.Tests.Web/` - 97 passing, incl. `DesignTokenTests`.
- **Real-browser check** (Playwright, 1600px viewport):
  - Before: `Category` cell width `47px`, `text-transform: none` - header reads "CategoryUE".
  - After: `Category` cell width `140px`, `text-transform: uppercase`, `category.right == due.left` (adjacent, no overlap). Header row reads `REF · TITLE · STATUS · PRIORITY · CATEGORY · DUE · CREATED`, all uppercase.

Note: one fix closes both issues since they are the same bug (#228 was filed with the detailed pointer; #214 predates it).

facts.title: feat(web): primary action button from SuggestedNextSteps (#211)
facts.description:
Closes #211.

`SuggestedNextSteps` was spent as a grey caption in the ticket header. The most likely next step should be a button that runs it.

## What changed
- **Contract enrichment (chosen approach, ADR 0041):** `SuggestedNextSteps` is now `IReadOnlyList<SuggestedStep>` - `(Text, SuggestedActionKind, TargetStatus?)`. The Application layer tags each step with the action it routes to (`None | ChangeStatus | Assign | Comment`) at generation time, where the reason for the suggestion is known. The client renders, it never parses the prose. Single source of truth; a server copy-edit can't silently turn a live button into a dead one.
- **Actionable steps ordered first**, so the "first step is the primary button" rule yields a live action whenever one exists, and only falls back to a caption when nothing is actionable (e.g. a Closed ticket). Adding a due date stays `None` (it's a details edit, not a routed action).
- **Ticket header:** the first step becomes the primary control - a button for a status change (executes it), an agent picker for assign - with the remaining steps behind an overflow menu (`⋮`). Unmapped steps render as non-clickable text.
- **Fallback:** no suggestions leaves the existing #208 generic controls, with no empty button. Every action calls the same `ITicketsApiClient` handler the manual path uses - no new automation, no new endpoint.
- Mapped the new enum in `TicketEnumMapping`; regenerated the OpenAPI snapshot and the ADR index.

## Interpretation note
The generic Change Status / Assign / Edit controls from #208 stay always-available (not hidden), so the suggestion primary is an additive recommended CTA and the generic controls are the ever-present fallback. This keeps the change non-regressive.

## Acceptance criteria
- [x] The primary button reflects the first suggested step and executes it.
- [x] A ticket with no suggestions falls back to the current generic action, with no empty button.
- [x] An unmappable suggestion is displayed, never clickable (overflow item disabled / caption text).
- [x] The action goes through the same command handler the manual path uses (`ChangeStatusAsync` / `AssignAsync` / comments tab → `AddCommentAsync`).

## Verification
- `dotnet build ./ServiceDeskLite.slnx -c Release` - warning-free; `dotnet test ./ServiceDeskLite.slnx` - all green (Api 267, EndToEnd 69, Web 97, Application incl. a new action-tagging test, …).
- **Real-browser E2E** (Playwright/headless Chromium against the running stack), on a New unassigned ticket:
  - Primary control reads **Assign an owner**; picking an agent assigns via the handler (sidebar shows `Alex Kim`).
  - After assigning, the primary becomes **Move to Triaged**; clicking it changes the status to `Triaged` (optimistic, same `ChangeStatusAsync` handler).
  - The overflow menu lists the remaining step as a clickable **Move to Triaged**; advisory `None` steps render disabled.

facts.title: feat(web): command palette on Ctrl+K (#210)
facts.description:
Closes #210.

A keyboard-first command palette that opens over any page, anchored on the power-user `Ctrl/Cmd+K` chord.

## What changed
- **`CommandPalette`** lives in `MainLayout`, so it is available on every page. A collocated JS module (`CommandPalette.razor.js`) adds a capture-phase `Ctrl/Cmd+K` handler that opens the palette even while a text field has focus, intercepting only that chord so ordinary typing is never swallowed.
- **Two result kinds**: navigation targets built from `NavRegistry` (not a second hard-coded list; section headers like *Admin* are excluded) and ticket hits from the existing search endpoint. `CommandPaletteEntries.Build` is the pure, unit-tested seam.
- **Debounced + cancellable ticket search**: each keystroke cancels the prior request via a `CancellationTokenSource` after a 200ms debounce, so only the newest query renders.
- **Fully keyboard operable**: arrow to move the selection, Enter to open, Esc to close. Esc also returns focus to wherever it was before the palette opened (saved/restored in JS).

Frontend only: no change to the search endpoint or any tool.

## Acceptance criteria
- [x] The palette opens from every page and does not swallow the browser shortcut when a text field has focus (capture-phase handler intercepts only Ctrl/Cmd+K).
- [x] Navigation entries are generated from `NavRegistry`, not a second hard-coded list.
- [x] Ticket search is debounced and cancellable.
- [x] Fully operable by keyboard: open, type, arrow, enter, escape.

## Verification
- `dotnet build ./ServiceDeskLite.slnx -c Release` - warning-free; `dotnet test tests/ServiceDeskLite.Tests.Web/` - 97 passing (5 new `CommandPaletteEntries` tests; design-token guard green).
- **Real-browser E2E** (Playwright/headless Chromium against the running stack):
  - `Ctrl+K` opens the palette showing 7 navigation entries (exactly the `NavRegistry` links).
  - Typing `Remote` yields 4 ticket rows with titles and refs (`#B29E72`, ...); `ArrowDown` + `Enter` navigates to `/tickets/{id}`.
  - Nav flow: typing `board`, `ArrowDown`, `Enter` navigates to `/tickets/board`.
  - `Esc` closes and returns focus to the previously focused app-bar search input (verified `document.activeElement` matches before/after).

## Follow-up (out of scope, noted separately)
The existing search endpoint matches `q` case-sensitively (`q=Remote` finds 4, `q=remote` finds 0). This is pre-existing server behavior shared with the app-bar search and the tickets list, not introduced here. Worth its own issue since it touches Infrastructure search across both persistence providers.

facts.title: feat(web): optimistic status updates with rollback on board and detail (#209)
facts.description:
Closes #209.

Every status change waited for the full server round trip; on the Kanban board the dragged card snapped back to its source column until the API answered. Status now renders immediately and reconciles with the server afterwards.

## What changed
- **`TicketBoardFeatureState.MoveAsync`** applies the target status to the card up front (optimistic), then on success reloads to reconcile with server truth (fresh allowed transitions), or on a rejected transition rolls back to the exact prior state. The rollback is local - a rejected move does not reload.
- **Concurrency guard**: a move sequence number ensures only the newest move reconciles. Two rapid changes on the same ticket cannot leave the board holding a status the server never accepted; a superseded older move passes its result through without touching state.
- **Detail view**: the status popover (added in #208) updates `_ticket` optimistically and restores the previous ticket if the server rejects.
- **Error surfacing**: both raise a snackbar carrying the ProblemDetails `code` (e.g. `[domain.ticket.status.invalid_transition]`), not a generic message. The board's inline `MudAlert` and its now-dead style are removed.

Scope: status only - ticket creation is untouched, per the issue.

## Acceptance criteria
- [x] A drag on the board updates the column before the response arrives (optimistic apply in `MoveAsync`).
- [x] A rejected transition (`TicketWorkflow`) rolls back to the exact previous state and explains why (snapshot restore + snackbar with the `code`).
- [x] Two rapid changes on the same ticket cannot leave the UI in a state the server does not hold (move-sequence guard; superseded move does not reconcile).
- [x] Covered by a Web test that fakes a failing / gated API client (3 new `TicketBoardFeatureState` tests).

## Verification
- `dotnet build ./ServiceDeskLite.slnx -c Release` - warning-free; `dotnet test tests/ServiceDeskLite.Tests.Web/` - 90 passing (17 board-state tests, +3 new).
- Live against the running API: an invalid transition (`New -> Closed`) returns `409` with `code: domain.ticket.status.invalid_transition` - the exact machine-readable value the snackbar now carries.
- The optimistic drag animation itself was not driven in a browser (no headless browser tooling here); the optimistic apply, rollback, concurrency guard, and error code are covered by unit tests and the live API rejection.

facts.title: feat(web): inline status and assignee edit instead of dialogs (#208)
facts.description:
Closes #208.

`AssignTicketDialog` and `ChangeStatusDialog` tore the agent out of the ticket into a modal for a two-field decision. Both are now inline popovers anchored to the header actions.

## What changed
- The **Change Status** and **Assign/Reassign** buttons are now `MudMenu` popovers. Picking an item applies the change immediately - the ticket stays open, scrolled, and on its current tab because only the in-place `_ticket` state updates. No navigation, no modal.
- The status menu lists the ticket's allowed transitions; the assignee menu lists the roster plus **Unassigned**, with a check icon marking the current assignee.
- Both call the same command handlers the dialogs used (`ChangeStatusAsync` / `AssignAsync` on `ITicketsApiClient`) - no new endpoint. Errors surface as a snackbar instead of a modal panel.
- `AssignTicketDialog.razor` and `ChangeStatusDialog.razor` are deleted, and the now-unused `IDialogService` injection is dropped.

No confirm dialog is added: neither a status nor an assignee change loses data, so per the issue the confirm dialog stays only where real data loss is possible (nowhere here).

## Acceptance criteria
- [x] Changing status or assignee never navigates or opens a modal.
- [x] Scroll position and any open tab survive the change (only in-place state updates).
- [x] The same command handlers are called as before; no new endpoint.
- [x] `AssignTicketDialog.razor` and `ChangeStatusDialog.razor` are removed.

## Verification
- `dotnet build` (web) - warning-free; `dotnet test tests/ServiceDeskLite.Tests.Web/` - 87 passing.
- Ran the full stack (API + Web, InMemory seeded): the ticket detail page renders with both popover menus and no exceptions; the deleted dialogs leave no trace in the markup.
- Exercised the exact endpoints the popovers call: status `New -> Triaged` returns the updated transitions, assign returns `Alex Kim`, unassign returns null.
- The live popover open/click was not driven in a browser (no headless browser tooling here); the render, the command path, and the component API are otherwise verified.

facts.title: feat(web): inline citation badges with hover preview in the assistant chat (#207)
facts.description:
Closes #207.

The assistant already streamed structured `AssistantCitation` values but the web rendered them as a flat "Sources" list, detached from the claim they support. This anchors citations to the answer text.

## What changed
- **`AnswerCitationLayout`** (new, pure/testable): splits a streamed answer into literal text runs and inline `[n]` badges by matching each citation's title in the answer text. The model cites by title per the system prompt (usually quoted), so the badge lands right after the closing quote and reads as `"Title" [n]`.
- **Inline badges** render where the model anchored a citation; **hover or keyboard focus** reveals a CSS-only tooltip with source, heading, and snippet. No JS, the trigger is focusable (`tabindex`, `role`, `aria-label`, `role="tooltip"`).
- **Numbered sources list** stays as the fallback for citations the model did not anchor inline. An answer with no citations renders unchanged, with no empty sources block.
- Citations arrive on the SSE `citation` event *before* the answer text that cites them, so they are buffered and attached to the next assistant bubble; a text-less turn still shows its sources.
- The grounding chip is untouched (ADR-0031 unaffected).

## Scope
Frontend only. No change to the assistant edge, the tools, or the SSE contract.

## Acceptance criteria
- [x] Citations render as inline badges where the model anchored them.
- [x] Tooltip shows source, heading, and snippet, and opens on keyboard focus too.
- [x] An answer without citations renders unchanged, with no empty sources block.
- [x] Grounding score chip stays where it is; this issue does not touch ADR-0031.

## Verification
- `dotnet build ./ServiceDeskLite.slnx -c Release` - warning-free.
- `dotnet test tests/ServiceDeskLite.Tests.Web/` - 87 passing, incl. 7 new `AnswerCitationLayout` tests (match, miss, mixed, duplicate titles, case-insensitivity, empty text).
- A live visual pass over a real citation flow needs an Anthropic + Voyage key and was not run here.

facts.title: docs(repo): add v1.8.0 release notes
facts.description:
Release notes and changelog for **v1.8.0 - Assistant Hardening: Grounding as a Mechanism, Honest Writes** (milestone M10).

- `docs/releases/v1.8.0.md` - full notes in the established format (summary, highlights, demo flow, included scope, known limitations, links)

Content: the release closes 5 of the 6 defects the v1.7.0 manual pass recorded (#190, #191, #193, #194, #195) plus the grounding strand (#186, #187/ADR-0039, #188/ADR-0040). #196 is named as moving with M9. facts.title: fix(assistant): write-honesty and confirmation policy in the system prompt (#190, #195)
facts.description:
Closes #190. Closes #195. Completes the M10 - Assistant Hardening strand.

One branch for both, deliberately: they are the two ends of one trade-off (a model made more cautious against #190 asks more useless questions, worsening #195), so they share a single confirmation policy. Genuine coupling, not incidental.

## Live reproduction first (real model, InMemory API, SSE)

| Field case (on `6f4297a`) | Today, before this change |
|---|---|
| #190 (a): "Setze die Priorität auf Critical" after create - confirmed with no call, twice | `update_ticket` fires immediately, confirmation after the result ✅ |
| #190 (b): reference resolution in a fresh conversation | searches honestly, asserts nothing ✅ |
| #195: needless double-confirmation | multi-write order executed without asking ✅ |

The #186 tool-description mitigation (with #187) resolved the field behaviour. **Not reproducible in five live turns covering both original paths.** What remained missing was the policy itself: the prompt never said when a confirmation is warranted (#195's explicit direction) or that execution must never be asserted without a result.

## What changed

One paragraph in the chat system prompt, two rules:

1. **Write honesty:** never state a change happened unless the tool call was made and its result reported success in this conversation - a claimed change the user later finds undone is worse than any error message.
2. **No needless confirmation:** when the user already asked for a change, make it - no re-asking, and no re-asking after correcting an earlier mistake. Asking before a write stays legitimate only for genuine user decisions: ambiguous ticket match, missing required info, hard-to-reverse action with real doubt about intent, or an uncertain `route_ticket` suggestion.

## Verified live against the new prompt

Including the exact field #195 scenario (scolding the model + "check it, then downgrade"): it verified via `search_tickets`, reported the evidence, then updated **without asking again** - the precise spot where the field session needed a repeated confirmation.

## Honest test boundary

Model behaviour cannot be pinned by the scripted evaluation suite - it would assert its own script (ADR-0037). Verification is the live pass above; the policy paragraph is the regression lock, in prose, at the one place both agents' chat turns read. Full solution stays green (574 tests), build 0 warnings.

## Side observation (not this PR)

`search_tickets` missed an existing ticket for one query phrasing while the REST search found it; a later, more specific query found it. Noted as a backlog observation, not filed - per the plan-before-issues discipline.

facts.title: fix(api): render summary timestamps in the user timezone (#194)
facts.description:
Closes #194. Third solo issue of the M10 - Assistant Hardening strand.

## Why

A comment written at 12:07 local time appeared in the streamed ticket summary as 10:07 - the CEST offset. The model faithfully repeated the UTC times the summary prompt fed it, contradicting the local timestamps the UI renders right next to the summary. The chat path already injects `Anthropic:UserTimeZone` (default `Europe/Berlin`) and has the model express times in that zone; the summary path did neither.

## What changed

- `BuildTicketPrompt` now takes the user timezone and converts every timestamp - created, due, each comment and event line - before it reaches the model. A header line names the zone explicitly so the model knows what it is reading.
- The UTC offset stays in the format string, so the model expresses due dates with the user's offset - the same rule the chat prompt demands for `dueAt` values.
- Same zone source as the chat path (`Anthropic:UserTimeZone`), resolved per request in `TicketSummaryService`.

## Acceptance criteria

- [x] Summary timestamps are rendered in `Anthropic:UserTimeZone`, matching the ticket detail view.
- [x] A regression test pins a fixed timezone (Europe/Berlin, summer date so CEST is part of the assertion) and replays the field case: 10:07 UTC renders as 12:07, and the UTC wall time must not leak into the prompt.

## Verification

- `TicketSummaryPromptTests` (+2). Full solution green (Api 267), `dotnet build -c Release` 0 warnings.

facts.title: feat(assistant): inject the agent roster into the system prompt (#193)
facts.description:
Closes #193. Second issue of the M10 - Assistant Hardening strand.

## Why

Asked to assign a ticket, the assistant correctly reported it has no way to list agents - and then invented one ("Morgan Davis" for Morgan Diaz). The roster reached the model only through the error path of `assign_ticket`, inside a failed call's message, where it got paraphrased. REST exposes `GET /api/v1/agents`; the assistant had no equivalent. Same failure class as #190, seen in a harmless place.

## What changed

Went with the option the issue proposes: **inject the roster into the system prompt** (five agents, negligible tokens, no thirteenth tool).

- The chat system prompt names the active roster per request, loaded through `GetAgentsHandler` - the same query `assign_ticket` validates against, so the prompt and the guard cannot disagree. An empty roster is stated, not omitted.
- The assign paragraph now says: use exactly these names, never infer or invent one, and when the user's name is not on the roster, list the valid ones instead of picking the closest match. The failed-call error path stays as fallback only.
- The worker prompt is untouched - the autonomous worker cannot assign (comment/status only).
- ADR-0025 notes `list_agents` as the replacement if the roster ever outgrows a prompt line.

## Acceptance criteria

- [x] The model can name the valid agents without a failed `assign_ticket` call first (roster is in the system prompt of every chat request).
- [x] README tool list and runbook stay accurate - no tool was added, both lists are unchanged and correct.
- [x] A test asserts the roster reaches the model: `RosterInPromptTests` reads the system prompt the loop actually sent upstream - all five seeded names present, "Morgan Davis" absent, and an empty roster is stated rather than omitted.

## Verification

- `Tests.Evaluation` 61 green (+2), full solution green, `dotnet build -c Release` 0 warnings.

facts.title: fix(api): report a failed knowledge-base search as an error (#191)
facts.description:
Closes #191. First issue of the M10 - Assistant Hardening strand.

## Why

`search_knowledge_base` caught a non-transient exception and returned it as a **successful** tool result (`IsError: false`). A failing Postgres query or a Voyage error was then indistinguishable from a clean search for every consumer:

- the dashboard counted it as a healthy invocation, understating the tool's error rate
- `ToolRetryPolicy` never saw a failure to classify
- "unavailable" (no Voyage key, by design) and "failed" (something broke) collapsed into the same user-facing outcome

`FindSimilarTicketsTool` already handled the identical case with `IsError: true`. The inconsistency was the defect. Latent, not field-observed: the manual pass ran on InMemory, which takes the honest `unavailable` path and never enters the catch.

## What changed

- The catch branch returns `IsError: true`, distinct from the honest `unavailable` degradation path (still `IsError: false`). Transient faults are still rethrown for `ToolRetryPolicy`, unchanged.
- The error flag flows to the dashboard (the invocation records `result.IsError`), so the error rate reflects real failures.

## Acceptance criteria

- [x] The catch branch returns `IsError: true`.
- [x] "Unavailable" and "failed" are distinct results with distinct messages (test asserts the contents differ).
- [x] The dashboard's error rate reflects technical failures (via `result.IsError` on the recorded invocation).
- [x] A unit test covers both branches (plus the transient-rethrow path).

## Verification

- `SearchKnowledgeBaseToolExecuteTests`: a technical failure is an error distinct from unavailable; a transient fault rethrows. Full solution green (Api 265). `dotnet build -c Release`: 0 warnings.

facts.title: fix(assistant): score grounding by meaning, not word overlap (#188)
facts.description:
Addresses #188. Fixes the measured defect (problem 1 of 2); problem 2 is called out below, not silently folded in.

## Why

The lexical `GroundingEvaluator` (ADR-0031) counted content-word overlap, so it failed exactly the answers that matter. Against the passage in `RagGroundingTests`:

| Answer | Old verdict |
|---|---|
| Verbatim restatement | Grounded |
| Hallucination | Ungrounded (correct) |
| Correct paraphrase | **Ungrounded** |
| Correct answer in German vs an English passage | **Ungrounded** |
| The exact hedge the prompt asks for | **Ungrounded** |

Latent until now, but ADR-0039 forces the check on every grounded answer, and any surfacing of the score would turn those false alarms into noise. A threshold does not help: a correct paraphrase scores 0.00, not 0.55.

## What changed

- `IGroundingEvaluator` port. `SemanticGroundingEvaluator` embeds each substantive answer sentence with the retrieved passages in **one** Voyage call and scores each sentence by cosine similarity to its nearest passage. A paraphrase or a translation sits close to the source it restates, where words did not match. Score (fraction of supported sentences) and verdict bands are unchanged from ADR-0031.
- `LexicalGroundingEvaluator` keeps the ADR-0031 algorithm and is the **fallback**: no Voyage key, or an embedding failure, degrades to it rather than returning no verdict. Grounding only runs after a KB retrieval, which already needs Voyage, so the fallback is the transient-failure net and the InMemory path.
- Sentences and passages both embedded as documents (one call). Threshold is a const calibrated for voyage-3.5.
- `CheckGroundingTool` resolves the port; DI wires the semantic evaluator with an optional `IEmbeddingClient` (absent on InMemory) and the lexical fallback.
- ADR-0040 supersedes the scoring decision of ADR-0031; README and runbook updated.

## Still open (problem 2 of #188)

Whole-answer scoping. Greetings, follow-up questions and ticket confirmations are not claims about the sources, yet the substantive-sentence heuristic counts any sentence with content words. It does not bite while `check_grounding` receives only the draft the model submits; classifying claim from non-claim is deferred until something grades a finished answer. Noted in ADR-0040. **This PR does not close #188 on its own** - suggest keeping it open for problem 2, or splitting it into a follow-up.

## Consequences worth noting

- The semantic path is **no longer deterministic** (two runs can differ). ADR-0031's determinism now belongs to the lexical path and the fixtures; the semantic path is tested deterministically via a fake embedder.
- Surfacing the verdict becomes defensible (the paraphrase/language false alarms are gone), but whether to surface it is a separate product decision, not taken here.

## Verification

- `SemanticGroundingEvaluatorTests` drive the meaning path with a fake embedder: paraphrase and German answer ground, a hallucination does not, and all three fallback triggers hold. No live call. Lexical fixture tests unchanged.
- Full solution green (Api 263, Evaluation 59, EndToEnd 69, ...). `dotnet build -c Release`: 0 warnings.

facts.title: feat(assistant): enforce the grounding check via tool_choice (#187)
facts.description:
Closes #187.

## Why

`check_grounding` was the only safety property in the assistant phrased as a prompt request. The system prompt asked the model to verify a KB-grounded answer, but `AgentLoop` did not require it, no guard demanded it, and `tool_choice` was never constrained. Every other bound is a mechanism (guard pipeline, handler validation, state machine, `HumanReviewGuard`). A skipped check failed silently: the answer streamed out unverified and looked identical to a verified one. Whether the model called it is model behaviour, which changes per release (#186), so a correctness property could not ride on it. ADR-0037's standard already named the failure: *"A rule the model can talk itself out of is not a rule."*

## What changed

- `AgentLoop` forces `check_grounding` through `tool_choice` once `IRagRetrievalContext` holds passages and no check has run this run. The model writes its draft into the tool's `answer` argument, so the verdict is computed **before the first streamed token**. After one check the model is free again (force-once).
- Injected `IRagRetrievalContext` into `AgentLoop` (both scoped). The bound holds for the interactive assistant **and** the autonomous worker, since they share the loop.
- The system prompt still asks for the check; a self-check satisfies the condition and skips the forced turn. Enforcement is the backstop.
- ADR-0039 records the decision; README updated.

## Deliberately out of scope (gated on #188)

The verdict is **not** surfaced to a user or a dashboard. The lexical `GroundingEvaluator` scores a correct paraphrase, a correct translation, and the exact hedging the prompt asks for all low. Forcing the check feeds those false alarms to the *model* (which can recognise its own paraphrase and answer anyway) rather than to a person. Surfacing waits on a semantic detector (#188).

## Force-once, not force-until-covered

The constraint fires once: the first turn after passages appear. It guarantees at least one grounding check after any retrieval. It does not guarantee every passage retrieved across a long chain was grounded before the final answer; the stricter invariant needs passage-delta tracking and is deferred until a run shows it is needed.

## Verification

- `GroundingEnforcementTests` asserts the `tool_choice` the loop actually sends upstream: forced after retrieval, not forced when the model self-checks, never forced without a retrieval, forced only once. Deterministic, no model call.
- Full solution green (`Tests.Evaluation` 59, EndToEnd 69, Api 257, Web 80, ...). `dotnet build -c Release`: 0 warnings.

Rejected: grading after the answer completes (too late, can only warn) and buffering until graded (gives up live streaming, ADR-0023).

facts.title: feat(web): design tokens - one scale for spacing, radius, elevation, and semantic color (#202)
facts.description:
Closes #202. The foundation every other issue in M9 depends on.

## What changed

`Theme/DesignTokens.cs` is now the single source for the palette, the spacing and radius scales, elevation, and the semantic chip colours. It renders them as `:root` custom properties into the document head - the same mechanism MudBlazor uses for its own palette - and `AppTheme` builds `MudTheme` from the same constants, so the two cannot drift.

All 16 scoped stylesheets and `wwwroot/app.css` read from the tokens. Gone: 297 colour literals, every raw spacing and radius value, four hard-coded monospace stacks, and the `--shell-*` block in `app.css` that was quietly a second source of truth.

## What the inventory turned up

- The status and priority chips were defined **three times** (queue, board, detail) and had already drifted apart: `inprogress` was `#fff5e6/#f3dfb7` in one file and `#fff4e2/#f1ddb2` in another. One token set now serves all three.
- 160 distinct colour literals, including `#7a8798`, `#7b8798`, `#7b8797` and `#7a8799` - hand-tuned greys with no system behind them.
- `--shell-border` and `--shell-font-mono` were used but never defined. Only their fallbacks ever rendered.

## API change

`KpiCard.Accent` was a free-form string naming a colour (`Accent="blue"`). It is now the `KpiAccent` enum naming a **tone** - `Info`, `Highlight`, `Caution`, `Critical`, `Positive`, `Neutral` - so a call site says what a number means rather than which colour it happens to use. The compiler immediately found the second call site in `AiInsightsPage`, where the tiles are "Tokens" and "RAG confidence" and a workflow-status name would have been wrong.

## Acceptance criteria

- [x] No hard-coded colour literal in any `Features/**/*.razor.css` or `Components/**/*.razor.css` - and none in `app.css` either, which the AC did not require but which dark mode (#203) would otherwise have had to patch in two places
- [x] Spacing and radius come from the token scale
- [x] `dotnet build -c Release` is warning-free; 585 tests pass
- [x] Before/after screenshots taken of dashboard, queue, board, ticket detail and assistant

**On "no visual regression":** spacing snaps to `4/8/16/24` and radius to `8/16/24` plus the pill, as the issue specifies. Roughly twenty distinct spacing values and eleven radii collapse onto the scale, so pixels move by one to four in places. That is the intended normalisation, not a regression; nothing else shifted.

`DesignTokenTests` reads the shipped stylesheets and fails on any colour, spacing, or radius literal. The scale now holds for the rest of the milestone rather than depending on review.

## Two fixes that fell out of the work

- **Board cards clipped their titles mid-glyph.** They are column-flex items and shrank past their own content; the tighter padding made it plainly visible, so `flex: 0 0 auto` lands here. While verifying, `-webkit-line-clamp` on those titles turned out never to apply either - Chrome blockifies `display: -webkit-box` on a grid item to `flow-root`. That needs a markup change and gets its own issue.
- The two undefined CSS variables above.

## Found, not fixed, filed separately

- The ticket queue header renders `Category` overlapping `DUE`, and unlike its neighbours it is not a sort label.
- The assistant composer's send button sits outside its panel.

Both predate this branch and belong in their own issues rather than folded in here.
